label: DAY 6
title: I made a game and let 4 bots play it 1,000 times. One never lost.

scenes.title: 4 bots. 1,000 games each.
scenes.caption: bot 4 playing
lines: I made a game, then let four bots play it a thousand times each. One of them never lost.

scenes.title: The rules
scenes.caption: how it plays
lines: The rules. Walls slide in, each with one gap. Move up, move down, or stay. Touch a wall and it's over.

scenes.title: Bot 1: the statue
scenes.caption: bot 1: never moves
lines: Bot one never moves at all. Over a thousand games, it averaged zero point two eight walls.

scenes.title: Bots 1 and 2
lines: Bot two moves completely at random. Zero point three. Basically a tie. About three in four games ended at the very first wall.

scenes.title: Bot 3: the chaser
scenes.caption: bot 3: heads for the gap
lines: Bot three, the chaser, heads straight for the next gap.
It averaged seven hundred twenty one walls, and 488 games hit my limit of a thousand. But it still lost 512 times.

scenes.title: Why the chaser lost
log: max it can move in time: 60
lines: Each time, the next gap was at the edge of what it could reach.
It moves sixty units before the wall arrives, plus eight of wiggle room in the gap. That gap was just too far.

scenes.label: bot 4: the planner
scenes.sub: games hit the 1,000-wall limit. zero losses.
lines: Bot four, the planner, also peeks at the gap after next, and slips through each gap on the side closer to it.
A thousand games. A million walls. It never touched one.

scenes.text: Looking one wall further ahead was enough.
scenes.sub: too easy now? tell me how to make it harder
lines: Looking one wall further ahead was enough. So my game is too easy. How should I make it harder? Tell me in the comments.
